citations.anchor: has exactly one plugin contributing a layout, and it is the shell
citations.why: Filters buildPlugins() for a `layout` and asserts the contributor list is exactly ['shell'], so a second layout contributor (or a non-shell one) fails.

citations.anchor: redirects a signed-out user from / to the sign-in page
citations.why: Pins the hazard the invariant names: with RequireAuth outside AuthProvider, useAuth falls back to Loading forever and RequireAuth renders the AppLoader, so the asserted redirect to /identity/signin never happens. AppShell's position inside the gate is not separately pinned.

citations.anchor: gives identity the only public routes, so the sign-in page renders outside the gate
citations.why: Asserts the set of plugins owning a `public` route is exactly ['identity'], so shell's `/` (or any shell route) carrying public:true fails. The second clause — the catch-all redirect being mounted inside the layout — is bootstrap-admin's and is not pinned here.

citations.anchor: is idempotent — running it again does not double anything
citations.why: Runs wireSlotContributions three times over the same contributions and asserts the slot still holds one item — exactly the hot-reload doubling the invariant forbids. That the wiring runs before the first render is bootstrap's ordering and is not pinned.

citations.anchor: does not drop an earlier contribution to the same slot
citations.why: Three contributions to one slot must all survive, which fails the moment `_reset` is folded into the registration loop instead of being a separate pass.

citations.anchor: does not let a consumer mutate the slot through the returned array
citations.why: Pushes, sorts and truncates the array getItems() handed back and asserts the slot's own contents are unchanged — the copy semantics the invariant states.

citations.anchor: keeps registration order for ties, so slot order is stable
citations.why: Pins the stability clause: equal `order` keeps registration order. The other clause — that the shell's sidebar/palette actually read their slots through byOrder, and the resulting Overview/Directory row order — is not pinned by any test.

citations.anchor: offers the Members nav entry only to someone who can read it
citations.why: Signs in with users:read and asserts the Members row is visible in the Primary nav, then with no permissions and asserts it is gone — the permission-gated half of the rule. The palette half (the same rule inside SidebarSearch) is not pinned anywhere.

citations.anchor: is the entry point, and opens a window focused on the composer
citations.why: Runs on a content-library route inside a workspace — where WorkspaceNav has taken over the sidebar's contextual area — and asserts the dock is on screen; CopilotLauncher is contributed only to SIDEBAR_FOOTER_SLOT, so a footer rendered inside the overridable region would unmount it and this fails.

citations.anchor: shows the signed-in account in the toolbar dropdown
citations.why: The other context: the same footer slot's AccountMenu asserted on a global route, where GlobalSidebar owns the contextual area.

citations.anchor: collapsing it from the keyboard hands focus to the reopen button
citations.why: Collapses from the panel's own Hide button and asserts the top bar's Show button holds focus — the collapse direction of the handoff.

citations.anchor: reopening it from the keyboard hands focus back into the panel
citations.why: The reopen direction: pressing the bar's Show button must leave focus on the panel's Hide button, which is the clause a collapse-only handoff would miss.

citations.anchor: a collapse the user never asked for is not persisted as a preference
citations.why: Stores 'open' on a wide viewport, reloads at 390px and waits for the collapsed-state Show button (so the panel started collapsed despite storage), then asserts localStorage still reads 'open' (so the forced value was not written back). Both clauses.

citations.anchor: Escape dismisses it
citations.why: The panel is role="dialog" on this breakpoint, so dropping the `:not(#app-right-panel)` exclusion makes the handler find the panel itself, yield, and leave Esc inert — the asserted collapse never happens.

citations.anchor: the scrim is decoration, not an unreachable control
citations.why: Asserts the scrim's tagName is not BUTTON, so reintroducing the hidden, keyboard-unreachable button fails. Its aria-hidden attribute is assumed by the locator rather than asserted.

citations.anchor: the first Tab reaches a visible skip link
citations.why: A single Tab from a freshly loaded private route must land on the skip link — i.e. it is the document's first focusable element — and it must be visible once focused.

citations.anchor: activating it puts focus inside main, past the sidebar
citations.why: Activating the link must move focus onto <main>, which only happens because the target carries tabIndex={-1} — the second clause.

citations.anchor: leaves the caret alone when a page search field has it
citations.why: Pins the ⌘K third of the invariant: with the caret in a page search box the palette must not open and the keystroke must reach the field. ⌘B and ⌘J are not pinned anywhere, nor is the claim that one shared function performs the check.

citations.anchor: closing it with Escape gives focus back to the trigger
citations.why: The restore half: closing without navigating puts focus back where it was.

citations.anchor: choosing a result does not drag focus back to the sidebar
citations.why: The deliberate non-restore half: after navigating from a result the sidebar's search trigger must not be focused.

citations.anchor: the sidebar is a named landmark
citations.why: Resolves the sidebar by role=complementary and the translated name 'Sidebar', so dropping or failing to translate the `label` prop fails. mobileTitle, mobileDescription and scrollLabel ('Page content') are asserted nowhere — the scrollport is only pinned as focusable, by data-slot, not by its name.

citations.anchor: activating it puts focus inside main, past the sidebar
citations.why: HostPage.main is page.getByRole('main'); a second <main> makes that locator resolve two nodes and toBeFocused() fails with a Playwright strict-mode violation.

shell:I-09.reason: Calling useHasPermission unconditionally is an implementation-shape rule (react-hooks/rules-of-hooks), not observable behaviour. Each nav row is its own component instance and `item.permission` is fixed for that instance's whole life, so a conditional call would never change the hook order within any single component and produces no difference a test harness could see — only lint can catch it.
